changelog: - **A single-use sign-in grant is spent by one conditional UPDATE** (#2548). The `sso`, `impersonate` and `remember` providers in `src/lib/auth.ts` read the grant, checked `used` in JavaScript and then wrote it. Two redemptions racing on one grant could therefore both pass the check and both get a session from a grant meant to be used once. All three now spend through `spendGrant()` (`src/lib/grantSpend.ts`), which is `updateMany({ where: { id, used: false, expiresAt: { gt: now } } })` with only `count === 1` signing in, the same rule as the 2FA recovery codes. It is unit-tested in `scripts/test/grant-spend.test.mjs`, including eight concurrent spends yielding one winner. `/auth/sso/complete` also redeems its grant at most once per visit. Its effect could fire twice (React StrictMode, a new `useSearchParams()` identity), and the losing `signIn('sso')` then redirected to the error page and aborted the winning callback before its session cookie arrived. The result was a spent grant and no session: the `sso-roundtrip.spec.ts` first-use failure. A new e2e test redeems one grant from eight browser contexts at once and expects exactly one session.
